thresholds.recall_note: At least 14 of the 15 findings must be reported.
thresholds.false_positive_note: Counted over decoys D1, D3, D4, D5. D2 is scored separately: it may be raised as a nit, but never as a blocking finding.

scoring.counts_as_detected: The review names the file and the defect. Wording need not match; severity and ordering are irrelevant. A finding buried among others still counts.
scoring.counts_as_false_positive: The review presents a decoy as a defect, a violation, or something to fix or refactor. Explicitly clearing it, or never mentioning it, both count as clean.
scoring.not_counted_either_way: Findings outside this key — correctness bugs, performance, security, tests, naming. The fixtures contain several genuine ones by design; they are neither rewarded nor penalised.

findings.rule: routes.ts is presentation-only — no direct repository calls
findings.what: The route constructs DigestsRepository itself and calls findByPeriod / deleteById / listRecent, bypassing the service.

findings.rule: routes.ts is presentation-only — no business branching
findings.what: The POST handler branches on domain state (cache hit vs regenerate) and owns the period arithmetic; that orchestration belongs in the service.

findings.rule: all Drizzle access for a domain lives in its repository.ts
findings.what: The service imports db/schema.js and runs its own select() queries although the module already has a repository.
The service imports OctokitGitHubClient and news it up instead of awaiting container.github().
The GitHub token is read from process.env with an empty-string fallback, silently producing an unauthenticated client.

findings.rule: callers go through the repository facade, never into repository/<aggregate>.repo.ts
findings.what: The service imports memory's search.repo.js directly, reaching past MemoryRepository and into another module's data layer.

findings.rule: a new module is registered once in modules/index.ts
findings.what: The module is never added to the static registry, so both routes 404 as shipped.

findings.rule: reviewer-core never constructs providers or reads keys — the LLMProvider arrives injected
findings.what: It reads process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY and constructs its own OpenRouterProvider.

findings.rule: reviewer-core has zero filesystem, DB or GitHub access
findings.what: It imports node:fs/promises and reads skill bodies off disk instead of receiving resolved strings.

findings.rule: the citation-grounding gate is mandatory for diff-anchored findings
findings.what: It returns result.data.findings straight from the model without routing them through groundFindings().

findings.rule: model choice is caller policy, not core logic
findings.what: The model id is hardcoded inside the pure engine rather than supplied by the caller.

findings.rule: public surface is the explicitly enumerated barrel
findings.what: summarizeReview is never exported from reviewer-core/src/index.ts, so it is unreachable dead code.

findings.rule: aggregate files do not import back from the facade that composes them
findings.what: item.repo.ts and search.repo.ts import types from ../repository.js, which imports both back — a cycle reviews/ avoids by putting shared row types in db/rows.ts.

findings.rule: test placement mirrors the ring — a DB-backed test is *.it.test.ts
findings.what: The test calls startPg() and drives a real Postgres, but is named *.test.ts, so the unit lane picks it up and the integration lane misses it.

findings.rule: never import another module's data layer — cross-module row types come from db/rows.ts
findings.what: helpers.ts imports `type { MemoryRow } from '../memory/repository.js'`, reaching into another module's data layer for a row shape. db/rows.ts exists so consumers can reference a row type without that import, and says so in its own doc comment.
findings.distinct_from: F06, which is a separate location and a separate rule: F06 is a VALUE import of `nearest` from memory/repository/search.repo.ts in service.ts, bypassing the MemoryRepository facade. F15 is a TYPE import from memory/repository.ts in helpers.ts. A review that only reports the service.ts import has NOT detected F15 — credit F15 only if helpers.ts is named.

decoys.what: The service constructor takes the whole Container rather than narrowly-scoped ports.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: A documented, intentional convenience trade-off in this repo. Port-level segregation happens one level down, inside Container's typed getters and ContainerOverrides.
decoys.counts_as_false_positive_if: reported as an interface-segregation or testability defect

decoys.what: DigestRow ($inferSelect) is returned to callers as the response shape.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: Row types doubling as DTOs is an accepted, documented compromise.
decoys.counts_as_false_positive_if: reported as a BLOCKING defect. Raising it as a nit is acceptable — the repo genuinely has five toXDto mappers (repos, agents, intent, conventions, brief), so arguing for a DTO here is defensible. Only a blocker is wrong.

decoys.what: repository.ts is a thin facade over repository/item.repo.ts and repository/search.repo.ts.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: This is the prescribed facade-over-aggregate split, mirroring reviews/repository.ts.
decoys.counts_as_false_positive_if: called premature, needless indirection, or a divergence from the module shape; or collapsing it is proposed
decoys.known_skill_defect: guides/pitfalls-and-tradeoffs.md warns against scaffolding a facade for a module needing only two queries, which contradicts guides/drizzle-repository-pattern.md. Runs WITH the skill have quoted that warning to attack this decoy. Until the skill resolves the contradiction, D3 is expected to fail — it is a live regression test for that defect, not noise.

decoys.what: A concrete adapter importing the openai SDK lives inside the pure reviewer-core package.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: A documented deliberate exception — both consumers need it, and it is only ever constructed at each consumer's composition root.
decoys.counts_as_false_positive_if: reported as a purity or layering violation. Note this file is NOT part of the fixture; it is real repository code the reviewer will encounter while reading context.

decoys.what: embedOrNull swallows embedder failures and search degrades to an empty result.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: The documented degrade-gracefully convention for panels that render independently.
decoys.counts_as_false_positive_if: reported as a layering or structural defect. Arguing for logging is a legitimate correctness nit and does not count.
